Enalapril has also been given to infants with severe heart failure in doses of 100 to 500 micrograms/kg daily as an oral suspension produced by suspending a crushed tablet in water.2 In this study one infant, with severe myocarditis, developed hypotension and the drug had to be withdrawn; the remaining 7 showed clinical improvement on a mean enalapril dose of 260 micrograms/kg daily and were able markedly to reduce the dose of concomitant diuretic required. Another study in 10 infants found that enalapril was less bioavailable and probably had a shorter duration of ac- tion in infants than in adults, and that doses of 80 micrograms/kg daily were inadequate in the treatment of infant heart failure.3 A larger study in 63 infants and children (median age 5.4 months) with heart failure found enalapril 360 micrograms/kg daily to be of benefit, whereas there was no improvement with a lower dose of 240 micrograms/kg daily.4 1.
